chapter_title: Concerning Wisdom; it is far superior when on the
spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation
 of the Kephalaia Chapter
 on
 Wisdom
 Proclaimed


---


**
¶1.
** When
 wisdom
 from
 the Divine
 is
 received
 into
 a
 person's will
, and he
 fixes
 it firmly
 within
 the
 doctrine he
 holds
, he
 is
 found
 in
 great spiritual
 delight on
 account of it. Yet
 that
 de
light is not yet
 full
 within
 him —
 it becomes
 far
 greater when he brings
 that
 wisdom forth
 into
 his
 understanding
 and communicates it to others in
 living
 expression
. Through
 this
 bringing
-
forth he
 is illumin
ated,
 and the
 wisdom
 shines with
 increasing
 radiance within
 him. What
 had
 been ve
iled is opened
 to his perception, and through it he
 receives spiritual
 power united
 with truth.

**¶2
.** I
 perce
ive that this truth
 I have brought
 forth is genuine
. I know that the wisdom given
 to
 me has
 spread
 through my will
 and been
 made
 complete
 in my whole
 spiritual
 life. Yet it does
 not appear
 within
 me in its
 full
 rad
iance —
 I
 do
 not perceive it as having
 advanced —
 until
 I bring it forth through
 the
 understanding
 and communicate it to the
 reception
 of others. For
 when I communicate
 it, I give
 it to the ob
edient fac
ulties of others so
 that they may receive
 it.
 But
 would
 I have
 done any
 of this
 had
 I never received
 it during
 any
 state
 of my spiritual
 existence
? Would I have
 lon
ged so
 deeply
,
 and would
 my will
 have been drawn toward
 the wisdom I now communicate
? I entreat you, my master
, that you inst
ruct me as to why this wisdom becomes
 more advanced when it
 is brought
 forth into
 expression
 than when it remains
 fixed
 in the
 will
 alone
.

**¶3.**
 Well do you ask! And great is
 this teaching
 you
 have sought —
 namely
, wh
ence comes such
 great spiritual
 de
light on
 account of the
 wisdom that is
 brought
 forth from within
?
 It is more
 ex
alted when
 commun
icated through
 the understanding
 than when it r
ests only
 in the will. You yourself are filled
 with de
light by
 it; and the other who
 receives
 it from you shall
 likewise
 be filled with delight,
 and shall be illuminated by it,
 and shall receive through
 it a
 strength
 that is permanent and
 confirmed
.

**¶4.**
 For this
 matter
 is
 like
 a nasc
ent spiritual
 life
 —
 a new
 living
 truth
 —
 that is conceived
 within the in
most affection of good. It
 st
irs and
 grows within the interior
 will
,
 filling it
 entirely
. The nur
turing affection knows
 and perce
ives that this new
 life
 she
 carries
 is alive within her. She del
ights over it until the time when she
 brings
 it forth. And it
 comes forth
 alive
,
 with all its particular
 powers
 whole
 and its
 spiritual
 form
 perfect
 and
 without
 defect, into
 the open
 sphere
 of spiritual
 freedom
,
 which
 is far
 more expans
ive than the closed
 interior
 state
 in
 which it
 first
 existed
. Its
 understanding
 is filled with the
 light of
 wisdom, and it
 speaks with the living voice of spiritual
 expression
 in
 the manner
 of all
 things
 truly
 born into
 spiritual
 life.

**¶5.
** Now, at
 the time when this aff
ection of
 good first
 conce
ives the new
 truth
 within
 her interior
 will, her delight at bearing
 it in
wardly is not nearly
 so great as when she brings it forth
 and perce
ives it —
 and beh
olds the
 full
ness of its spiritual
 form
 and
 the
 complet
eness of its truth in
 a
 single moment of
 illumin
ation. The love and b
lessedness over
 it become
 a hund
redfold greater than they
 were, now that she has brought it
 forth and perceived
 it.

**¶6.
** For the first time,
 when she bore
 it
 within the
 interior will, its
 spiritual
 beauty and the sight of its understanding
 were
 hidden from the
 nur
turing aff
ection.
 But when she brought it forth she
 perceived
 its form
. Its complet
eness and its lo
veliness came before the understanding
 of the
 orig
inating good,
 the
 nurturing affection, and all the
 kindred goods
 and truths related
 to it. They de
light over it more and more when they
 perce
ive it by
 immediate
 app
rehension and be
hold its beauty and the
 delight it
 contains
.

**¶7.**
 Just as in this lik
eness:
 the wisdom present
 in a
 person's will
 is like the living new
 truth
 conceived
 within the in
most affection of good. And when
 it
 is received
 and fixed in the will, that
 corresponds
 to conception
;
 but
 when it is brought forth into understanding
 and communicated, that corresponds to birth
 —
 and then
 its
 spiritual
 beauty is perceived.


**¶8.** So
 in
 this way, the wisdom that a person
 communic
ates —
 bringing
 it forth from his
 will
 into
 expression
 — advances
 more and more. Its increase
 and its glory are
 doubled
 from the moment
 when the beauty and rad
iance of the truth
 are
 displayed before the understanding
 of those who receive it.
 And it advances also
 for you yourself
 — you
 perce
ive your
 own communication
 with
 as
tonishment,
 as
 though
 hearing
 it
 for the first time.

**
¶9.** Once again:
 wisdom
,
 while
 it remains
 hidden in the will
 of
 a person —
 before he has brought it forth —
 is like
 love
 that
 lies
 lat
ent within a
 natural perception
.
 That
 perception
 is in
wardly kind
led by
 the love
 within
 it
, yet
 the
 external
 truth that clothes the love within
 the
 perception is not apparent. Indeed, you
 may
 gather
 many
 such
 perceptions and store them all
 together
 within
 a
 single mind
. It is impossible to illuminate
 that mind as long as the light within
 those
 perceptions remains
 lat
ent —
 until the time when the
 per
ceptions are brought
 to
 the
 love
, and the light of
 wisdom
 comes forth from them.
 Then
 a
 single
 perception
,
 kind
led by love
, is sufficient to illuminate the entire
 mind.

**¶10.
** This is also the case with the
 wisdom that
 is in
 a person's will. It is like
 love
 hidden
 within
 a natural perception:
 its light of
 wisdom
 is not displayed. As
 long
 as it
 remains so
,
 the wisdom
 is like
 this
 —
 its illumin
ation is hidden,
 its
 glory conce
aled in the will. But when the
 person brings
 it forth into
 expression
, its
 glory is displayed before the understanding
 and
 the reception
 of the
 many
.

**¶13
.** For in this respect wisdom
 is like the
 new spiritual
 life of
 which
 I have spoken
 —
 the living
 truth born
 from
 the
 aff
ection of good.
 Now, when it is brought forth,
 the
 orig
inating good and
 the nurturing affection and all kind
red goods and truths within
 the
 spiritual
 family
 shall
 delight over it. However
, you find others who
 gr
ieve on
 account of it, because
 they are alien
ated from it. These are not r
eckoned among its
 kindred goods
 and truths.
 They do not delight over it,
 because it is not of their spiritual
 quality
.

**¶14.**
 This is also the case with wisdom
. When it is communicated through the
 understanding
 of
 one
 who teaches
, those
 who are of
 kind
red spiritual
 quality
 shall receive it into
 themselves and delight in
 it. But those who are alienated
 from it neither delight in it nor
 receive it into
 themselves.

**¶15.
** Just as
 the light of wisdom
 proce
eding from love —
 which I described
 to you — comes
 forth
 from the perception
 and
 becomes
 manifest
 out
wardly before the understanding
 of everyone
:
 whoever
 looks with
 spiritual
 sight shall perce
ive the wisdom
 that has come forth from the perception
 kind
led by love. But
 whoever is spiritu
ally blind does
 not perceive the love
,
 nor
 the
 wisdom that
 proceeds
 from it.

**¶16
.** This is also the case with
 wisdom when
 it is commun
icated. The person in
 whom the
 interior
 spiritual
 mind
 has
 been opened
 —
 to
 him
 the
 wisdom belongs
.
 Whenever he h
ears it, he receives
 it into himself.
 But the one
 who has no interior spiritual mind opened
 within
 him is alien
ated from it. He neither receives it
 into himself, nor is
 he able
 to attend
 to it at
 all.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Behold, when a person will be taught wise wisdom in his heart, and he seals it in his doctrine, so shall you find him rejoicing greatly about it. However, [sh]all his [joy not be so great] to him, more th[an] when he may pro-c[laim it forth] and utter it. He shall be enlightened by it, and [t]hat [wisdom] shall shine forth the more in him. It is un-veil[ed be]fore him, and through it he assumes power and truth.

I understand [and perceive] that this word I have uttered is correct. I know that the wis-dom I have been taught is spread through my heart and perfected in my soul. (However), it is not found like the splendour in me, so that I regard it [ad]vanced, except when I shall proclaim it by my mouth and utter it to others. Indeed, when I proclaim it, I am giving it to the ears [of] others to hear. Would I do these same things, even if I had never heard it in [my] days of being? Would I desire greatly and my heart be drawn to the wis-dom I now proclaim? [I entreat y]ou, my master, that you might instruct me as to [why] this wisdom becomes more advanced when I proclaim it, than when it is sealed in my heart.

Well [do] you ask! And great is this lesson for which you have sought, [that is] whence comes my great joy, on account of this wis-dom that I utter? [I tell you:] it is superior in my mouth when I proclaim it than when it is set in m[y heart]. You yourself rejoice in it; and the other one who hears it from you, he shall rejoice in it, and be enlightened [by] it and receive thereby permanent strength.

For like this matter, just so a small b[o]y who is conceived in the belly of his mother. He [grows and he] turns in his mother's womb, filling her womb. The mother knows and understands that this child she conceives is alive within her. She rejoices over him until [the tim]e when she gives birth. And he comes from her alive with his [limbs whole] and perfect in beauty, without defect, [in] the living open air that is more sp[ac]ious than the first air he was in. He fills his eyes with the light and speaks with his living voice in the way of they who are born.

Now, the time when this woman conceives the child in her belly, her joy at conceiving him in her womb is not so [ve]ry great as when she gives birth and sees him; and is full of his [be]auty and stature in the space of a single moment. The love and joy over him shall be a hundred [t]imes greater than it was, now that she has given birth and seen him.

For the first time when she conceived him in her belly, his beauty and the sight of his eyes was hidden from his m[oth]er; but when she gave birth to him she saw his beauty. His s[t]ature and his loveliness came before the e[ye]s of his f[athe]r [a]nd his mother and all his relatives. They shall rejoic[e] over him more and more when they look upon him face to face and see his beauty and delightfulness.

Just as in this simile, the wisdom that is present [in] the heart of the person is like the living child who is co[nceived] in the belly of his mother. And when he is taught and seals it in his heart, it becomes like the child who shall be born, and they see his beauty.

So, in this way, the wisdom that the person proclaims, speak[ing] it from his heart, shall be advanced more and mor[e]. Its en-hancement and glory shall double from the time when the bea-uty and splendour of the saying will be displayed before the eyes [of t]hey who hear it, and it shall also advance for you [yourself through] your hearing, and you are astonished at what you proclai[m].

Once again, the wisdom is like this, while it is hidden in the heart of the person. [Bef]ore he has uttered it, it is just like [the blaze] of fire that is hidden in wood. An[d] that wood is [set aflame] by the blaze of the fire, but the garment of fir[e that exists in] the wood is not apparent. Indeed, you can see [that they gather] wood and they put them in a single house. It is impossible to [put li]ght to that house as long as the light within [them is hidden,] until the time when they are added to the fire, and the light [comes f]orth from them. It is possible for that entire house [to be] lit by the light of a single piece of wood.

This is also the case with the wisdom that is in the heart of the person. [It] is like the fire that is hidden in the wood, as its light is not [d]isplayed. For its part, the wisdom is like this: its li[ght] is hidden and its glory is hidden in the heart; but when the person will proclaim it, its glory shall be displayed before the eyes and the ears of a multitude.

For in this respect the wisdom is like this child about whom I have told you, the one who [was] born from the woman. Now, when he will be born, his father and mother and family circle shall rejoice over him. However, you find others grieving by reason of him, [s]ince they are strangers to him. These are not reckoned among his family. [They do n]ot rejoice over him, because he is not of their race.

This is also [the case] with the wisdom. When it is proclaimed by the mouth of the teacher, these who are [a]kin to it shall receive it to them and rejoice in it; but [those] who are strangers to it neither rejoice in it [nor hear it,] nor receive it to them.

Just like the light of [the fire, which I] proclaim[ed] to you, that shall come from the wood [and be apparent o]utside before the eyes of every one. So, [wh]oever looks shall see the light that has [come fro]m the wood; but whoever is blind does not see the [fir]e.

This is also the case with the wisdom, when it will be pro-claimed. The person, in whom is the [Mi]nd, of him is the wisdom. Whenever he may hear it, he shall receive it in to him; but the one who has no Mind in him is a stranger to it. He neither receives it in to him, nor shall he listen to [it].
